description: The verb table: the ONE home for what a tracker verb is called, what it takes and what it prints. scripts/tracker.sh validates a verb against this file BEFORE it resolves a backend, so a typo is a bad invocation (exit 2) on every host rather than 'not implemented' (exit 3) on some. `skills` names, per migrated skill, the verbs that skill needs — it is empty until the first skill moves its own gh calls onto the contract, and `tracker.capable` reads it to answer whether a skill can run on a host. See skills/_shared/tracker-contract.md.

verbs.stdout: one verb per line — the backend protocol's own introspection call, answered without gh, a network or a host resolution

issue-view.stdout: {"number","title","state","body","labels","url","format"} — state lower-cased, labels as bare names

issue-search.stdout: [{"number","title","state"}] — state lower-cased. A search with --label and no --query is valid.

issue-comments.stdout: a JSON array of comment bodies

issue-create.stdout: {"number","url"} — a label not in the live set is passed through and the host FAILS the whole call (exit 1), exactly as `gh issue create --label` does today; the caller checks the live set first

issue-edit-body.stdout: nothing — refuses a missing or empty --body-file (exit 2) and sends nothing

issue-reopen.stdout: nothing — the file is the reopening comment

label-create.stdout: nothing — grows the taxonomy for a genuinely new sub-area with no fitting label

issue-link-parent.stdout: ok | fallback | FAILED (HTTP <code>: <message>) — a 404 means the sub-issues feature is off on this host, not that either issue is missing (both are resolved by a successful read first); --dry-run prints the POST it would send and calls nothing

issue-link-blocked-by.stdout: ok | fallback | FAILED (HTTP <code>: <message>) — same rule as issue-link-parent, on the dependencies endpoint

issue-children.stdout: a JSON array of issue numbers, or fallback when the sub-issues feature is off

issue-blocked-by-count.stdout: an integer, or n/a when the dependencies feature is off (no issue_dependencies_summary on the issue)

pr-create.stdout: {"number","url"} — refuses a missing or empty --body-file (exit 2) and sends nothing, and on Azure DevOps a description over 4000 characters too. GitLab marks a draft with a `Draft: ` title prefix, Azure DevOps with isDraft. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

pr-list.stdout: [{"number","title","url","state","isDraft","headBranch","body","mergedAt","mergeStateStatus"}] — state lower-cased open|closed|merged, headBranch a bare name, mergedAt null until the PR merges; mergeStateStatus is pr-merge-state's word for the PR (null where the host does not answer it in a list: callers fall back to pr-merge-state); --search matches the PR body

pr-view.stdout: {"number","title","url","state","isDraft","body","headBranch","baseBranch","headSha","author","mergedAt","mergeSha"} — state lower-cased, branches as bare names, author a login; mergedAt and mergeSha null until the PR merges (#752: guarded-pr-merge.sh reads the outcome back through them)

pr-edit-body.stdout: nothing — refuses a missing or empty --body-file (exit 2) and sends nothing, and on Azure DevOps a description over 4000 characters too. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

pr-ready.stdout: nothing — flips a draft PR ready; GitLab strips the title's Draft: prefix and leaves a non-draft MR alone. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

pr-commits.stdout: a JSON array of the PR's commit SHAs — added by #751 because pr-existence-guard.sh breaks a tie between open PRs closing one issue by commit count (#214), and no other verb prints commits

pr-merge-state.stdout: {"behind_by","mergeStateStatus","isDraft","reviewDecision","unresolved_threads"} — GitHub's words, UNKNOWN for a state the host cannot map; unresolved_threads lists the paths of unresolved threads ((pr-level) for a thread with no path). Exit 1 with nothing printed when any of its reads fails

pr-checks.stdout: [{"name","state","bucket"}] — bucket is pass|fail|pending|skipping|cancel. No checks prints [] and exits 0; a host error is exit 1, never []

commit-checks.stdout: [{"name","state","bucket","id","app","html_url"}] — every run on the sha, not reduced (ci.verdict reduces); state in GitHub's lower-case check-run words (conclusion // status), or UNKNOWN. A host error is exit 1, never []

pr-threads.stdout: [{"id","path","line","body","isResolved"}] — one entry per review thread, its first comment's path, line and body. A failed read is exit 1, never []

pr-thread-resolve.stdout: nothing — posts the file as a reply, then resolves the thread. Refuses a missing or empty --body-file (exit 2) and sends nothing. Added by #752: merge-pr resolves threads and must never resolve one silently. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

pr-merge.stdout: nothing — the exit code is a hint, never the verdict: read the outcome back through pr-view. Refuses a missing or empty --body-file when one is given (exit 2). --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

branch-delete.stdout: ok | gone — gone when the branch was already deleted. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

issue-parent.stdout: the parent's number, none, or fallback when the host cannot say (the sub-issues feature off). A parent in another repository exits 1 (#781)

pr-closing-issues.stdout: a JSON array of the issue numbers the PR closes — added by #752 because merge-pr Step 5c reads them and no other verb prints them

issue-list.stdout: [{"number","title","labels","body","comments","createdAt","blockedBy","blocking","subIssues","assignees"}] — labels bare names, assignees logins, comments an array of bodies or null when the host does not fetch them. Each edge is {"nodes":[{"number","state"}],"totalCount"} — state OPEN, CLOSED or null when the host's list does not say — or null when the host has no such relation. A failed read exits 1 and prints nothing. Added by #753: auto-dev's survey reads the open backlog through it

issue-assign.stdout: ok | already-assigned — assigns the authenticated user. Added by #753: auto-dev holds a replan issue by assigning it, and no other verb writes an assignee. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing

pr-comment.stdout: nothing — refuses a missing or empty --body-file (exit 2) and sends nothing. Added by #752: merge-pr records observations as a PR comment. --dry-run prints one DRY-RUN line and calls nothing
